subject: Proposal: discrete-burst commitment options and activation cadence — MedQuBe
messages:
From: Liam O'Reilly <liam@medqube.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops+procurement@medqube.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing question for dedicated cluster proposal

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday — the pilot looked promising. Our procurement team asked for a written proposal that shows concrete reservation options and the activation cadence so they can budget for Q3. Specifically they want:

- A baseline reserved cluster option (min guaranteed GPUs) with price and SLA
- A staged ramp path (month-by-month activation schedule) if we want to start small and scale to peak
- A discrete burst mechanism (how many burst GPUs, seconds/minutes per hour allowed, cost) tied to the reserved pool

We have a target of ~6M inference tokens/day at 8k concurrency for peak clinical workloads, and want to understand the tradeoffs between committing to a 32-GPU pool vs starting at 8 and ramping.

Can you send a concise set of options we can circulate? Procurement would like a PDF and a quick cost workbook.

Cheers,
Liam
--
Liam O'Reilly
VP, Platform
MedQuBe
liam@medqube.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing question for dedicated cluster proposal

Liam — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching two artifacts: a two-page proposal PDF (MQ-Reservation-Options-v3.pdf) and a cost workbook (cost-model-mq-v2.xlsx). Below are the three high-level reservation paths with the key trade-offs so procurement can review quickly.

1) Predictable Reserve (Committed 32-GPU pool)\- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 32 (pinned to your account)\- Activation: immediate, fully provisioned in dedicated pool\- Typical workload fit: steady high throughput (6M tokens/day + sustained concurrency)\- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 120ms for generation requests (model dependent)\- Pricing: lower per-token unit cost (discount vs staged paths)\- Pros: simplest billing, no activation risk; Cons: higher up-front commit

2) Staged Ramp (8 -> 16 -> 32 over 3 months)\- Month 1: reserve 8 GPUs (baseline for pilot and initial prod)\- Month 2: add 8 GPUs (16 total) once throughput crosses 40% of projected peak\- Month 3: add 16 GPUs (32 total) when telemetry shows stable ramp and latency under SLO\- Billing: monthly billing based on reserved pool size that month\- Pros: aligns spend with growth; Cons: requires automated scaling windows and small risk of transient throttles during rapid spikes

3) Flexible Reserve + Burst Lanes (8 reserved + 24 burstable)\- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 8\- Dedicated burst lane: ability to borrow up to 24 GPUs from a shared burst pool for short intervals (configured per hour)\- Burst policy example: up to 24 GPUs for up to 10 minutes per hour, or 6 GPUs continuous for the hour (customizable)\- Pricing: blended model with a small premium on reserved units + usage-based charge for burst minutes\- Pros: much lower committed spend, preserves ability to handle production spikes; Cons: burst availability is not 100% guaranteed during global contention windows (we provide fallback to smaller model variants)

Next steps I recommend: review the attached PDF (page 2 has the activation cadence variants) and we can lock a preferred path for the quote. Ben is cc'ed — he can provide the detailed throughput anchors and a quick runbook for autoscaling and KV-cache warmup.

Best,
Kimberly

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: 2027-04-19T11:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing question for dedicated cluster proposal

Hi team — quick answers inline: 

1) Lead times for staged add-ons:
\- Provisioning window: typically 24-72 hours to activate additional GPUs once the order is placed (this assumes dedicated capacity availability in region).
\- Configuration + warm-up: 2–12 hours for model binary distribution, shard placement, and KV-cache priming (we recommend a short warm traffic window to validate SLOs).

2) Burst lanes billing:
\- Burst usage is consolidated on the same monthly invoice as the reserved charges for clarity. Burst minutes are listed as a separate line item with minutes and effective per-minute rate.

3) Minimum contract length:
\- Predictable Reserve (32-GPU): standard 12-month commitment with monthly billing; 24-month option available for additional discounting.
\- Staged Ramp: month-to-month for each increment with a 3-month minimum term for any added capacity above baseline (to avoid churn on transient add-ons).
\- Flexible Reserve + Burst: 6-month minimum on the reserved portion; burst is pay-as-you-go.

Operational notes: we recommend enabling prefix caching and a gradual canary traffic ramp when adding GPUs to avoid KV cache misses and to achieve the latency SLOs quickly. Aditya — can you confirm the default burst policy values and whether we can provide a guaranteed burst reservation for a fee?

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter

ben_carter@redwood.com

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Folks — following up on Ben's note. For this size of workload (target ~6M tokens/day, peak 8k concurrency), our recommended operational knobs: 

- Baseline: start with staged ramp (8->16->32) so you validate telemetry without overcommitting. The cost-model workbook shows crossover at month 4 where committed 32 becomes cheaper overall if you sustain peak.
- KV warmup: we recommend a 4–8 hour scheduled warmup window after each GPU add (run synthetic traffic using your prompt corpus).
- Burst policy options:
  * Default: 24 GPUs burst for up to 10 minutes per hour (best-effort)
  * Guaranteed short-burst: reserve an additional 8 GPUs as guaranteed burst for an incremental monthly fee (we can price this in the updated PDF if you'd like guaranteed headroom)
- Autoscaling hook: we provide a webhook + console action where your orchestrator can trigger additive activation; we also support automatic policy (threshold-based) with a 15-minute cool-down.

I'll update the PDF with a sample 3-month activation calendar and two example invoices (one for staged ramp, one for flexible + burst) and push it to the HubSpot deal record. If you want the faster procurement path, I can prepare a DocuSign-ready quote with the 12-month 32-GPU commitment and the optional guaranteed 8-GPU burst.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk procurement through the workbook.

-Aditya
